en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its near-perfect symmetrical cone shape that observers can easily see from Legazpi City.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller crater lake observable during clear weather.
The giant Rafflesia flower found in the forests of Bukidnon can grow up to 80 centimeters wide and smells like rotting meat.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over a thousand cone-shaped limestone hills that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine eagle, observable in the montane forests of Mindanao, has a distinctive crest of long, dark brown feathers on its head.
During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool northeast monsoon winds that bring dry weather to most of the country.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, featuring observable mossy forests and rare endemic plants near its summit.
The Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City features twin waterfalls dropping 97 meters, powered by the Agus River for hydroelectricity.
The Philippine tarsier, observable in the sanctuaries of Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
The Pink Beach in Zamboanga City gets its distinct color from red organ pipe coral fragments mixed with white sand.
Mount Pinatubo in Zambales features a stunning caldera lake that formed inside its crater after its massive eruption in 1991.
